subject: Request: logo + case-study permission in exchange for expanded discount
messages:
From: Sofia Delgado <s.delgado@acmehealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Marketing partnership question

Hi Marcus,

Thanks again for the overview last week — the trial data looked promising. Our procurement team has asked whether Redwood would consider a larger introductory discount (we're asking for 40% off list for the first 12 months) in exchange for a co-marketing package: logo permission for use on Redwood's website, a 1-pager joint case summary after 3 months, and a short customer quote we can sign off on.

I've attached Acme's logo usage guidelines and a draft visibility matrix so you can see what we'd expect. If this is something Redwood can do, we can fast-track PO and signatures. If not, let me know what concessions would make this workable on your side.

Cheers,
Sofia Delgado
Head of Partnerships
Acme Health
[s.delgado@acmehealth.com]

Attachment: Acme_Logo_Guidelines.pdf
Attachment: Proposed_Visibility_Matrix.xlsx

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Delgado <s.delgado@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketing partnership question

Hi Sofia — really appreciate the clear ask and the artifacts.

Short answer: we're open to a visibility-for-discount trade, but any publicity/case study permission requires approvals from Marketing and Deal Desk (and sign-off on the final quote). Laura and Marissa, looping you in to review the proposed scope and logo usage guidelines.

Operationally I want to avoid a blanket 40% concession without structure. Could Marketing confirm what Creative/PR resources are required, and Deal Desk/legal confirm whether we need additional indemnities / approval steps? If agreed, we can structure a 20% standard discount with an additional conditional 20% promotional allowance tied to: (1) signed marketing release, (2) approved quote/attribution, and (3) publication within 6 months.

Sofia, if that conditional approach works we can reflect it in the SOW and expedite the PO.

—Marcus
Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment: SOW_v3.pdf

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sofia Delgado <s.delgado@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketing partnership question

Thanks for flagging this, Marcus. Reviewed Acme's guidelines and the visibility matrix. High level: Acme is a good fit for a customer spotlight — we can commit to a 1-pager and a web case tile plus social amplification. A few caveats:

- We need a final approved quote/attribution and a signed marketing release (standard Redwood template with minor edits).
- Creative will need ~8 hours of design + 4 hours of PM time; estimate ~$2.5k in internal effort (we can absorb for strategic accounts).
- We should avoid logo lockups or claims implying endorsement beyond a factual case study. Legal needs to sign the release.

If Deal Desk is comfortable with a conditional discount tied to those deliverables, Marketing can commit. Marissa — can you confirm whether the 20%+20% split above is acceptable from a deal economics perspective?

Laura Bennett
Head of Marketing, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Sofia Delgado <s.delgado@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 08:16:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketing partnership question

Marcus / Laura — quick notes from Deal Desk: the standard pricing deck only goes to 30% for inaugural enterprise discounts. To hit 40% economics on year one we need either a multi-year commitment (2+ year revenue commitment) or exec approval for a promotional allowance.

Given Acme's ARR profile and strategic fit in healthcare, I'm willing to recommend the conditional approach: 20% baseline discount plus a one-time promotional allowance of 20% (applied to first-year invoice) contingent on: signed marketing release (Legal-approved), publication within 6 months, and inclusion on our customer list for events. This would be a non-recurring concession and would be recorded in the deal comments.

Requesting exec approval from Aditya for the additional 20% promotional allowance (non-recurring). Aditya — can you OK this exception if Legal signs off on the release?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Sr Deal Desk Manager
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Sofia Delgado <s.delgado@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketing partnership question

Thanks for the context. I approve the one-time 20% promotional allowance for deal DW-ACME-4532 under these conditions:

1) Legal signs the standard marketing release with only minor redlines (no indemnity expansion).
2) The promotional allowance is non-recurring and applied only to the first-year invoice.
3) Marketing confirms publication plan and timeline (target within 6 months).
4) The SOW and invoice language explicitly reflect the conditional nature of the concession.

Marissa — please capture this approval in the deal record and issue the approval memo to Procurement. Marcus — please share the redlined release from Acme once available; Laura / Creative to prep assets after legal sign-off.

Aditya Rao
VP, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com
